name: ffsubsync
role: CLI that shifts an existing subtitle file to match the speech in audio or video, without ASR
summary: Python CLI `ffsubsync`: aligns an SRT or other subtitle file to a video, audio file or reference subtitle by matching voice activity to cue timing, applying one offset and an optional framerate scale. It does not transcribe or fix drift across cuts.
use_when: A caption file is a constant offset from the speech after a re-edit or a new voiceover take
Retiming without transcription; whisperx and syncalong make new timings by ASR
avoid_when: Timing that drifts across cuts: one offset cannot fix it
Producing timings from audio: whisperx or syncalong

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install ffsubsync==0.5.1

notes: 2026-11-27: lead said `uv tool install`; the fixture uses a pinned venv instead. PyPI 0.5.1 (2026-07-24) matches the lead, MIT. Requires ffmpeg on PATH and pulls pysubs2, numpy, webrtcvad-wheels and auditok.

2026-11-27: on a 30 s clip the default 60 s offset search chose -23 s for a +3 s shift and dropped cues with negative times; --max-offset-seconds 5 or 10 found the right offset. Cause not established.

assessment.rationale: PyPI 0.5.1 uploaded 2026-07-24, MIT per installed metadata; the last push was four months ago. Nothing catalogued corrects the timing of an existing caption file without ASR: whisperx and syncalong re-time by transcribing, caption-checker only checks, pysubs2 shifts by a number you must already know.

evidence.result: 7 `say` phrases at known times on a 30 s track; SRT shifted +3.0 s and -1.5 s. With --max-offset-seconds 10 both are corrected, worst start/end error 0.01 s (limit 0.25 s). With default flags both FAIL: offset -23 s chosen for +3.0 s, 2 and 1 of 7 cues returned. Two processes identical. Python 3.12.13.
evidence.scope: Constant offsets on clean synthetic speech, 30 s; default-flag checks fail and are recorded (KNOWN FAIL). No drift, music, real recordings, framerate or reference-SRT sync; macOS arm64.
